title: Power/Performance Curves: INT8, AWQ, GPTQ exploratory benchmarks
content:
Objective:
Run an exploratory set of field-style benchmarks to map power (GPU wattage), throughput (tokens/sec), tail latency (95/99p), and a small set of accuracy proxies (perplexity on eval prompts, top-k token divergence) across quant formats and kernels. Primary formats: INT8 (our stable kernel), AWQ (variant we onboarded last quarter), GPTQ (reference). Secondary: FP8 runs for sanity. Goal is a practical curve (power vs throughput vs quality) to inform: kernel routing heuristics, autoscaler power targets, and Dedicated capacity sizing guidance.

Motivation / context:
- We have many microbenchmarks focused on latency/throughput at fixed batch sizes. What we don’t have is a consistent mapping that includes power consumption (for Dedicated customers that care about unit economics and power-availability on private deployments) and quality regressions across quant types under realistic mixed workloads.
- Some customers are asking: if we switch to AWQ for cost reasons, what is the expected power drop and how much quality do we give up? This doc is a quick scoped investigation to give rough numbers and hypotheses.

Hardware & baseline config:
- GPUs: NVIDIA A100 80GB (driver 525), sample H100 runs for comparison (driver 555) where noted.
- Host: 64 vCPU, 256GB RAM.
- NVML used for instantaneous power sampling (250ms resolution).
- Nsight Systems (nsys) for a subset to correlate kernel runtime with power spikes.
- Serving runtime: branch: power-probe-2025 (PR 3890) — instrumentation for power logging + token timestamps.
- Models: redwood-3b (dense), redwood-7b (baseline medium), and a small open LLM for cross-check (gpt-small-ish) — all converted to matching quant formats.
- Workloads: short chat-like (prompts 32 tokens, gen 64), long context (context 4k tokens, gen 512), bursty mixed (50% short, 30% medium, 20% long).
- Batching: dynamic batching enabled; experiments run with target batch windows 5ms, 15ms, 50ms to see batching effect on power/throughput.
- KV cache warm vs cold: two modes for each test (cold start no cache, steady-state warmed cache).

Methodology / measurement notes:
- Each datapoint = median of 5 runs, each run 3000 requests (or 30 minutes for long context).
- Record per-GPU power (avg and stddev), tokens/s, 95p/99p latencies, and quality proxies: ppl on a 200-prompt eval set and top-1 token divergence rate vs FP32 baseline.
- For AWQ/GPTQ we used recommended kernel configurations from kernel team; we also forced kernel switchover (fast-fallback) to measure overhead.
- For INT8 we tested two kernel implementations: our standard vectorized kernel and an alternate cache-friendly kernel (kcache).
- Power normalization: reported watts as delta above idle (idle measured after boot and warm OS, no model loaded).

Key results (high level):
- Throughput vs power tradeoffs (short prompts, A100, warmed cache):
  - INT8 (vector kernel): 11.8k tokens/s, +95W (delta), ppl +0.9% vs FP32; 95p latency 42ms.
  - INT8 (kcache kernel): 10.6k tokens/s, +82W, ppl +0.9%; 95p latency 48ms (more stable under burst).
  - AWQ: 13.2k tokens/s, +78W, ppl +2.6% vs FP32; 95p latency 46ms (tails slightly elevated under mixed bursts).
  - GPTQ: 12.1k tokens/s, +88W, ppl +1.7%; 95p latency 44ms.
  - FP8: 13.5k tokens/s, +105W, ppl +1.1% (note: FP8 increased power vs AWQ/INT8 due to kernel inefficiencies on A100).

- Long-context (4k ctx, gen 512), steady-state:
  - INT8 (vector): 2.1k tokens/s, +140W, ppl +1.2%.
  - AWQ: 2.6k tokens/s, +128W, ppl +3.5%.
  - GPTQ: 2.3k tokens/s, +135W, ppl +2.1%.
  Observations: AWQ retains the throughput lead for long contexts but quality delta is larger. KV cache behavior amplifies AWQ instability in some sequences (see "edge prompts" below).

- Mixed workload (burst profile) notes:
  - AWQ showed the lowest average power per-token, but had occasional 200-400ms tail spikes correlated with kernel fallback events when attention lengths in the batch diverged. These spikes caused 99p to jump by 2x in our burst test.
  - INT8 kcache kernel had fewer spikes but lower peak throughput (less aggressive vectorization).

- Throughput per watt metric (tokens/s per watt delta):
  - AWQ: ~169 tokens/s/W (short prompt)
  - INT8 (vector): ~124 tokens/s/W
  - GPTQ: ~137 tokens/s/W
  - FP8: ~129 tokens/s/W (despite higher throughput, higher power penalizes per-watt)
  Note: numbers vary with context length and batching window.

- Quality proxies:
  - AWQ consistently has the largest top-1 divergence vs FP32 on the 200-prompt eval set (2.1% avg divergence), with variance driven by a small subset of prompts that include long numeric sequences / repeated spans.
  - GPTQ is generally between INT8 and AWQ in divergence but more stable across prompt types.
  - Perplexity correlates with top-1 divergence but the effect size is smaller (percentage-level changes).

Micro-observations / interesting cases:
- Edge prompts (reproducible set of ~8 prompts) caused AWQ kernels to fall into a different attention-shape kernel that had poor memory locality; showed up as clear NVML power spikes and kernel context switches in nsys traces. Reproducible: ticketed as ENGINF-1431 (investigate kernel shim).
- Kernel switchover costs: forcing switchover mid-request (simulated mismatch between routing decision and actual attention pattern) costed ~250ms in median for long contexts in AWQ; INT8 fallback path was ~80ms — explains tail behavior.
- H100 runs: AWQ appears more efficient on H100 (throughput up 12% and power stable), narrowing the power-per-token gap. That suggests HW affinity differences drive some of A100 inefficiency.

Hypotheses / explanations:
- AWQ gains throughput by more aggressive packing / vectorization but relies on heuristics for attention-shape selection; when heuristics miss, kernel fallback costs are large and quality can degrade for certain patterns.
- INT8 vector kernel is conservative (less packing, better stability) — better for tight SLOs where tails matter.
- FP8 has higher raw throughput but our A100 kernels are not yet optimized, resulting in worse per-watt.

Actionable recommendations (short term):
1) Add power-aware routing policy prototype: prefer AWQ for steady long-context traffic when customer allows +/- 3% quality drift, prefer INT8-kcache for bursty/sloped traffic where 99p matters. (P0 to prototype in 2 sprints)
2) Kernel telemetry: instrument the kernel selection decision path to log failed heuristic counts + estimate switchover overhead. Link to ENGINF-1431. (P0)
3) Dedicated capacity sizing doc: include tokens/s-per-watt numbers per quant/kernels for A100 and H100 to help capacity planners. (P1)
4) Investigate AWQ fallback optimization: work with kernel team to reduce mid-request switchover cost (target <120ms). (P0)
5) Add a small per-customer "power budget" flag on Dedicated to route queries to lower-power kernels when requested; prototype via routing rule. (P2)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How much of AWQ instability is dataset-specific (numeric/repetition heavy)? Need a larger prompt corpus (2k) representing customer traffic.
- FP8 kernel optimization roadmap for A100 — coordinate with driver/kernel team. Is it worth prioritizing?
- Autoscaler: can we expose power as a first-class metric for scaling decisions (e.g., maintain avg watt < X)? What is the control surface?

Quick TODOs / next experiments:
- Run 2k-prompt AWQ stress on H100 vs A100 (clearer hardware affinity) — Diego to run by 2025-11-14.
- Add kernel selection logging patch to master with minimal perf impact — Priya to PR by 2025-11-12 (linked PR 3890 is the initial instrumentation).
- Create a small "edge prompt" dataset and fuzz attention shapes to reproduce fallback paths deterministically — Eli owns.

Appendix: reproducibility notes
- Branch: power-probe-2025, run harness: tools/bench/power_probe.py with flags --model redwood-7b --quant {int8,awq,gptq,fp8} --batch-window {5,15,50} --workload {short,long,mixed} --nvml-sample-ms 250. Script writes per-token timestamps + nvml logs to /tmp/power_runs/<runid>.
- Nsight trace template: traces/awq-power-template.qdrep (be careful with nsys overhead; only sample 1 run per config).
- Eval prompt set: evals/200_small_prompts_v1.txt (internal).

Notes to reviewer:
- This is exploratory and not exhaustive; numbers are approximate and meant to expose operational tradeoffs. We should decide which curves to formalize into an official benchmark matrix.
- Feedback: which dimension is most useful to product (power vs cost vs SLO)? I suspect Dedicated / Private customers will prioritize per-watt economics, Hosted customers will care more about 99p tails.

End of notes.
